mission.beneficiary: Couples and close friends who routinely stay together in Discord voice channels until bedtime and want an automatic, privacy-preserving exit.
mission.consequential_choice: sequence: defer final loop selection, test the nightly exit scheduler first, select it only if repeat-use and reliability thresholds survive, otherwise reject it and pivot to the next bounded observed-behavior probe
falsifiers: Fewer than 25% of activated users schedule exits in at least three separate weeks.
Successful execution remains below 99% across restarts, reconnects, timezone changes, channel switches, and permission changes.
Manual departures, cancellations, or last-minute modifications dominate scheduled executions.
Users characterize the problem as only mildly annoying or find scheduling more cumbersome than disconnecting manually.
Mistaken or unwanted disconnects create material participant complaints or interpersonal harm.
The active server population is not meaningfully composed of users with recurring bedtime voice-channel behavior.
mission.interpretation: The nightly voice-channel exit scheduler is the most reversible and evidence-aligned candidate because it matches the original concrete problem, avoids speech capture and generative-AI costs, and can be piloted narrowly. It does not yet survive selection: README prominence is not demand evidence, and real-world repeat use and execution reliability are unknown.
mission.mission: Defer product-loop selection and run a bounded four-week pilot of dependable scheduled voice-channel exits to determine whether couples and close friends exhibit a recurring, valuable habit.
mission.next_probe: Instrument schedule creation, confirmation, modification, cancellation, manual early departure, execution, failure reason, and weekly repeat use; recruit 10–20 relevant Discord pairs; test restarts, reconnects, timezones, channel changes, and permissions; then interview repeaters, abandoners, and anyone affected by an erroneous disconnect.
non_goals: Selecting the conversational voice assistant before measuring demand, latency, trust acceptance, and sustainable per-turn cost.
Expanding music, newsletter, AI-chat, or bulk voice-channel orchestration features during the pilot.
Using cloned voices, retaining speech, recording conversations, or transmitting voice data to generative services.
Treating upstream TEN VAD or Voicebox claims as GahyeonBot production evidence.
Generalizing pilot results beyond the recruited beneficiary cohort without follow-up evidence.
mission.rationale: This probe offers the highest information gain at the lowest integration, privacy, trust, and operating-cost burden. It tests the strongest candidate without committing to broad positioning. Voice assistance is comparatively slow, costly, fragile, and trust-sensitive; group orchestration risks coercive bulk actions; music is commoditized; and newsletters are disconnected from the original voice-channel problem. Selection should follow observed repetition and reliability rather than feature descriptions.
mission.situation: GahyeonBot spans unrelated scheduling, music, newsletter, AI-chat, and voice-assistant features, but the frozen packet contains no observed usage, retention, latency, trust, reliability, or operating-cost evidence sufficient to select a durable repeat loop.
mission.success_signal: Among 10–20 recruited Discord pairs, at least 25% of activated users schedule exits in at least three separate pilot weeks, scheduled executions succeed at least 99% of the time across realistic lifecycle and permission conditions, and interviews show the automation materially improves on manual disconnection.

candidate_critiques.disconfirming_evidence: Few activated pairs repeat scheduling across three weeks; cancellations and last-minute modifications dominate executions; users commonly leave manually before the scheduled time; interviews rate the problem as mildly annoying; or reliability remains below 99% under realistic lifecycle and permission changes.
candidate_critiques.failure_mode: The original anecdote may describe a rare inconvenience rather than a durable nightly habit. Scheduling commands may be more cumbersome than manually disconnecting, recurring schedules may not match variable bedtimes, and execution reliability can degrade across reconnects, restarts, timezones, permissions, and users switching channels.
candidate_critiques.hidden_harm: A mistaken disconnect can interrupt intimate or important conversations, create interpersonal conflict, or remove the wrong participant. Achieving 99% reliability may consume disproportionate engineering effort for a narrow, low-value action, while couple-focused positioning limits growth and may expose sensitive relationship-pattern metadata.
candidate_critiques.mission: Dependable nightly voice-channel exit scheduler for couples and close friends.

candidate_critiques.disconfirming_evidence: Observed communities perform qualifying actions less than weekly; manual coordination is already fast; fewer than 30% of hosts repeat within four weeks; participant complaints are material; permission failures exceed 5%; or established moderation tools already satisfy the need.
candidate_critiques.failure_mode: The workflow may occur only during occasional events, while Discord permissions, channel structures, participant roles, and consent requirements make supposedly reusable actions server-specific. Hosts may prefer verbal instructions or existing moderation bots, and members may resist automated movement or dismissal.
candidate_critiques.hidden_harm: Bulk actions can become coercive moderation tools, disrupt parallel conversations, move uninvolved users, or amplify mistakes across an entire group. Permission and consent UX could grow into a complex policy system whose maintenance exceeds the value of infrequent coordination.
candidate_critiques.mission: Lightweight voice-channel orchestration for community hosts who gather, move, or dismiss groups.

candidate_critiques.disconfirming_evidence: Median response latency exceeds 2.5 seconds or p95 exceeds 5 seconds; false activations exceed one per user-hour; transcription or playback failures are common; users reject microphone or cloned-voice consent; per-turn cost exceeds a predetermined sustainable limit; or fewer than 20% return weekly after novelty fades.
candidate_critiques.failure_mode: The serial VAD, 1.2-second endpointing, STT, model, TTS, and playback path may be too slow and fragile for natural conversation, especially with crosstalk, music, echo, packet loss, cold starts, and concurrency. Novelty may produce initial usage without retention, while explicit activation and consent reduce adoption.
candidate_critiques.hidden_harm: This candidate would waste the most effort if wrong because it requires the broadest integration, observability, infrastructure, safety, consent, and latency work before demand is established. It also introduces microphone surveillance concerns, transcript and voice-data exposure, cloned-voice impersonation risk, false activations, unpredictable costs, and disruption of human conversation.
candidate_critiques.mission: Hands-free conversational companion for fast, trustworthy speak-and-hear Discord interactions.

candidate_critiques.disconfirming_evidence: Users cannot name a painful incumbent deficiency; command-to-playback latency is not competitive; fewer than 30% of first-session servers return within two weeks; collaborative queues do not improve satisfaction; or source and policy constraints prevent reliable playback.
candidate_critiques.failure_mode: Music bots are a mature commodity, so reliable basic controls may not create switching motivation. Search, streaming-source restrictions, licensing changes, queue disputes, and playback reliability can dominate development while incumbents retain stronger recognition and integrations.
candidate_critiques.hidden_harm: The project could spend substantial effort chasing provider breakages and parity features without differentiation. Shared controls can also create conflict, abuse, or moderation overhead, while legal and platform-policy exposure may threaten the entire loop independently of product quality.
candidate_critiques.mission: Fast shared music-control layer for small Discord voice groups.

candidate_critiques.disconfirming_evidence: Four-week retention falls below 35%; meaningful interaction stays below 20%; first-week mute or unsubscribe exceeds 15%; interviews reveal users prefer existing sources; content errors erode trust; or cost per retained subscriber is unsustainable.
candidate_critiques.failure_mode: The loop may optimize delivery rather than value: users can subscribe impulsively, ignore messages, and mute the bot as notification fatigue grows. Broad topics lack differentiation from existing newsletters, feeds, and platform alerts, while meaningful DM open measurement may be unavailable or misleading.
candidate_critiques.hidden_harm: Unwanted DMs can damage trust in the entire bot, generate spam complaints, and create moderation or platform-policy risk. Finance, travel, or news summaries can be stale or incorrect, and personalization plus engagement tracking introduces data-governance burdens disconnected from the bot's original voice-channel purpose.
candidate_critiques.mission: Consent-based recurring personalized briefing service delivered through Discord DMs.

shared_assumptions: A single narrow repeat loop is preferable to a portfolio of features, even though the packet contains no evidence that heterogeneous demand is itself the problem.
README prominence and original framing are useful proxies for real user pain, adoption, or current product usage.
The documented features are sufficiently implemented and production-ready to pilot, despite truncated artifacts and no operational evidence.
Discord users will install a bot, grant the required permissions, learn its controls, and trust it enough for the proposed workflow.
The proposed beneficiaries actually dominate the active server base; no server, session, or demographic data establishes this.
Four-week pilots and the proposed thresholds are long enough and correctly calibrated to distinguish novelty, seasonality, and durable retention.
Instrumentation can accurately measure success, engagement, consent, and failures without itself creating privacy or trust problems.
Reliability, latency, trust, and cost can be evaluated independently, although weakness in any one may suppress observed demand for the others.
Local inference materially improves privacy or economics, despite shifting burden to hardware, cold starts, capacity planning, maintenance, and deployment complexity.
Existing Discord behavior and competing bots leave enough unmet need for any candidate to earn repeated use.
Users experiencing a problem frequently will prefer automation over existing manual workarounds.
The absence of analytics, interviews, traces, error rates, and costs is merely an evidence gap rather than evidence that none of the proposed loops has achieved meaningful use.

interpretations: A narrow bedtime voice-channel exit loop may be the strongest candidate because it addresses the clearest recurring problem in the original product framing and can operate without users trusting speech capture or generative AI.

A coordinated group-exit or voice-channel orchestration loop may be more socially valuable than individual scheduling because Discord behavior is group-centered, but the packet does not establish how frequently this situation occurs.

A hands-free conversational voice-assistant loop could create higher engagement through repeated speak-and-hear turns, especially with VAD, local STT, and personalized TTS; however, its latency, privacy, reliability, and operating-cost burden are substantially higher.

A music-control loop could already fit habitual voice-channel use and avoid some AI trust concerns, but the packet gives no differentiation, usage evidence, or indication that it solves an underserved problem.
Newsletter subscriptions could produce a predictable recurring DM loop, but this appears disconnected from the bot’s original voice-channel problem and risks becoming generic broadcast functionality.

The breadth of documented features may reflect experimentation before product focus rather than demonstrated demand; alternatively, it may reflect actual heterogeneous user demand that the packet simply does not quantify.
Local Voicebox integration may reduce marginal API cost and improve privacy, but it may shift costs into model hosting, hardware, maintenance, cold-start latency, and deployment complexity.
VAD gating may materially control false requests and cost, but silence-based endpointing plus STT, model generation, and TTS may still make the conversational loop feel slow in Discord.
Personalized cloned speech could make the assistant distinctive and emotionally engaging, or it could increase consent, impersonation, and trust concerns that suppress adoption.

A narrow loop should not be selected from this packet alone because the required decision explicitly depends on observed Discord behavior, latency, trust, and operating-cost evidence, none of which is supplied at decision quality.
missing_evidence: Per-feature usage counts, unique users, repeat frequency, retention, and abandonment rates across scheduled exits, group exits, music, newsletters, AI chat, and voice assistance.
Direct observation or interviews showing which Discord situations recur, how users currently solve them, and which problem they consider painful enough to adopt a bot for.
Cohort data distinguishing novelty use from durable weekly or nightly habits.
End-to-end latency distributions for VAD endpointing, STT, OpenRouter first token and completion, TTS generation, and Discord playback, including cold starts and concurrent load.
False-positive, false-negative, interruption, empty-audio, transcription-error, and failed-playback rates in real Discord environments with music, crosstalk, echo, and packet loss.
Operating cost per active user and per completed voice turn, including API charges, local inference hardware, bandwidth, storage, monitoring, and engineering maintenance.
Capacity and concurrency limits for local Voicebox/STT deployment and evidence that production infrastructure can meet acceptable response times.
User trust evidence covering microphone capture, voice-data retention, third-party transmission, cloned-voice consent, impersonation risk, and willingness to enable the assistant.
Clear privacy, consent, deletion, moderation, and abuse-handling policies for voice recordings, transcripts, generated responses, and cloned profiles.
Comparative completion time and satisfaction for command-based scheduling versus conversational voice interaction.
Evidence that scheduled exits execute reliably across restarts, reconnects, timezone changes, Discord permission changes, and deployment transitions.
Competitive analysis showing whether music, newsletters, or general voice-assistant functionality is differentiated enough to drive repeat use.
The actual number and type of active servers, voice-channel session patterns, user demographics, and whether couples, friend groups, communities, or administrators dominate usage.
A controlled pilot comparing candidate narrow loops on activation, successful completion, repeat rate, latency tolerance, trust acceptance, and cost.
Complete, untruncated implementation and operational documentation sufficient to verify whether the described features are production-ready or merely configurable intentions.
observations: GahyeonBot currently combines several unrelated feature families: scheduled voice-channel exits, group exits, reservation management, music controls, newsletters, AI chat, and a voice assistant.
The original README framing describes two concrete Discord voice-channel situations: leaving a channel automatically at bedtime and gathering or moving multiple voice users for an announcement.
The documented voice-assistant loop is VAD-triggered speech detection, silence-based turn finalization, STT, one streaming OpenRouter request per utterance, and TTS playback.
Voice-assistant, STT, and OpenRouter capabilities are disabled by default, while VAD defaults to enabled when the assistant is active.
The system exposes configurable VAD threshold and end-of-speech silence duration; the documented default silence duration alone adds about 1.2 seconds before downstream processing begins.
The README claims VAD prevents background noise and empty Discord audio packets from generating STT or OpenRouter requests, indicating explicit concern about false activations and usage cost.
The voice path depends on multiple components and credentials: Discord audio, TEN VAD, an STT service, optionally OpenRouter, and Voicebox or another TTS provider.
Voicebox supports local STT and TTS, voice cloning, multiple models, and long synthesis, but the packet provides no evidence that Discord users want these capabilities inside GahyeonBot.
TEN VAD is presented by its own project as accurate, lightweight, low-latency, and available for Java, but these are upstream claims rather than measurements from GahyeonBot.
The supplied artifacts contain feature descriptions and configuration details but no observed usage analytics, user interviews, retention data, latency traces, error rates, or cost measurements.
The artifact packet is nearly byte-budget-limited and all three excerpts are truncated, so relevant implementation or operational details may be absent.

candidate_missions.beneficiary: Couples and close friends who routinely remain in a voice channel until bedtime and want a low-friction, privacy-preserving way to leave automatically.
candidate_missions.falsifier: Reject this mission if a four-week pilot shows fewer than 25% of activated users schedule exits on at least three separate weeks, or if successful scheduled execution remains below 99% across restarts, reconnects, timezone changes, and permission changes.
candidate_missions.mechanism: Let users create, confirm, modify, and cancel one-time or recurring exit schedules with minimal commands, then reliably disconnect the intended participants at the scheduled time without recording speech or invoking generative AI.
candidate_missions.mission: Make GahyeonBot the dependable nightly voice-channel exit scheduler for couples and close friends who fall asleep together on Discord.
candidate_missions.next_probe: Instrument scheduled-exit creation, cancellation, execution, failure reason, and weekly repeat use; recruit 10–20 relevant Discord pairs for a four-week pilot and interview both repeaters and abandoners.

candidate_missions.beneficiary: Discord moderators, event hosts, gaming leaders, and study-group organizers who repeatedly coordinate multiple voice participants.
candidate_missions.falsifier: Reject this mission if observed servers perform qualifying group-coordination actions less than weekly, fewer than 30% of activated hosts repeat the workflow within four weeks, or permission and consent failures affect more than 5% of attempted actions.
candidate_missions.mechanism: Provide permission-aware group actions with previews, participant consent where appropriate, clear confirmations, and reusable event presets for announcements, study sessions, games, and closing routines.
candidate_missions.mission: Make GahyeonBot a lightweight voice-channel orchestration tool for community hosts who need to gather, move, or dismiss groups during live Discord sessions.
candidate_missions.next_probe: Observe 8–12 active communities during real events, log current manual coordination steps, and pilot a single gather-or-dismiss workflow while measuring completion time, repeat frequency, participant complaints, and permission failures.

candidate_missions.beneficiary: Discord users who want accessible hands-free assistance or social AI interaction without leaving an active voice session.
candidate_missions.falsifier: Reject this mission if median end-of-speech-to-audible-response latency exceeds 2.5 seconds, p95 exceeds 5 seconds, false activations exceed one per user-hour, completed-turn cost exceeds the sustainable target established before the pilot, or fewer than 20% of consenting users return weekly after novelty use.
candidate_missions.mechanism: Use TEN VAD for speech gating, silence-based turn detection, STT, one streamed model request per utterance, and local-first Voicebox TTS, with explicit activation, visible listening state, interruption controls, and strict voice-data retention settings.
candidate_missions.mission: Make GahyeonBot a hands-free conversational companion that can sustain fast, trustworthy speak-and-hear interactions inside Discord voice channels.
candidate_missions.next_probe: Run an opt-in pilot that separately traces VAD endpointing, STT, model first token, TTS, and playback; measure false activations, transcription failures, interruptions, per-turn infrastructure cost, consent acceptance, and four-week retention.

candidate_missions.beneficiary: Small friend groups and gaming parties that listen to music together and need predictable shared controls.
candidate_missions.falsifier: Reject this mission if fewer than 30% of servers that complete a first playback session start another session within two weeks, median command-to-playback latency is not competitive with existing bots, or users report no meaningful advantage over their current music bot.
candidate_missions.mechanism: Concentrate on reliable join, search, play, pause, skip, queue, and collaborative control flows, with clear playback state and lightweight voting or host policies instead of adding general AI features.
candidate_missions.mission: Make GahyeonBot the fastest shared music-control layer for small Discord voice groups.
candidate_missions.next_probe: Instrument complete playback sessions and command latency, interview servers already using competing music bots, and test one differentiator—such as frictionless shared queues—in a two-week comparative pilot.

candidate_missions.beneficiary: Discord users who want recurring technology, AI, finance, sports, or travel briefings within Discord rather than another standalone newsletter app.
candidate_missions.falsifier: Reject this mission if four-week subscriber retention is below 35%, fewer than 20% of delivered briefings produce a meaningful open or interaction signal, unsubscribe or mute rates exceed 15% in the first week, or content-generation and delivery costs cannot be covered sustainably.
candidate_missions.mechanism: Offer explicit topic subscriptions, predictable delivery schedules, concise summaries, source controls, pause and unsubscribe actions, and engagement feedback without coupling the loop to voice-channel features.
candidate_missions.mission: Make GahyeonBot a consent-based recurring briefing service that delivers narrowly personalized Discord DMs users consistently read and act on.
candidate_missions.next_probe: Pilot one topic with 50 opt-in users, measure subscription completion, delivery engagement, saves or follow-up actions, unsubscribe timing, weekly retention, and cost per retained subscriber.
